content: Butorphanol nasal spray is prescribed to alleviate moderate to severe pain and is also used to manage migraine headaches. It may sometimes be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. The medication is delivered via a pump and is typically administered as one spray into one nostril. If pain relief is not achieved within 60 to 90 minutes, another single spray may be used. This two-dose sequence can usually be repeated every 3 to 4 hours as needed. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Before using butorphanol for the first time, read the written directions provided by the manufacturer. The pump must be primed if it has not been used for 48 hours or longer. A single bottle provides approximately 8 to 10 doses if priming is required or 14 to 15 doses if no priming is needed between uses. To use the pump, follow these steps: 1. Wash your hands thoroughly. 2. Gently blow your nose to clear your nasal passages. 3. Remove the clear cover and protective clip from the bottle. 4. If priming is needed, aim the nasal sprayer away from people and animals, and pump the spray bottle firmly and quickly (up to eight strokes) until a fine mist appears. 5. Insert the tip of the sprayer approximately 1/4 inch into one nostril, pointing it toward the back of your nose. 6. Close the other nostril with your finger and tilt your head slightly forward. 7. Pump the spray firmly and quickly once, and sniff gently with your mouth closed. 8. Remove the sprayer from your nose. 9. Replace the protective clip and cover on the spray bottle. Use butorphanol nasal spray exactly as directed. There is a small risk of the drug being habit-forming. Do not use a larger dose, use it more frequently, or use it for a longer period than prescribed by your doctor. Before using butorphanol nasal spray, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to butorphanol or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other pain relievers, antidepressants, medications for cough, cold, or allergies, nasal sprays, sedatives, sleeping pills, tranquilizers, and vitamins. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had liver, kidney, lung, or heart disease. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using butorphanol nasal spray, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are using this medication. Be aware that this drug may cause drowsiness or dizziness. Avoid driving or operating machinery for at least one hour after using butorphanol and until you no longer feel drowsy or dizzy. Alcohol can exacerbate the drowsiness caused by this drug, so you should not consume alcohol while using butorphanol. If you forget a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not use a double dose to make up for a missed one. Butorphanol nasal spray may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: Drowsiness Lightheadedness Dizziness Upset stomach Vomiting Headache Nasal congestion Runny nose Sore throat Ringing in the ears If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: Difficulty breathing Fainting Irregular heartbeat If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. After each use, replace the protective clip and clear cover on the spray bottle and return it to its child-resistant container. Store the medication at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication. Consult your pharmacist about the proper disposal of your medication. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the victim has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with anyone else. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
